sections.title: What the bot can do
sections.menu: Every feature in one place
sections.intro:
A Discord bot for **Roblox** game creators: you run your game straight from Discord. Promo codes, eggs, multiplier events, gifts, on-screen announcements and bans reach the game within seconds, without publishing it. You configure everything on Discord, without editing files.

The bot speaks **English, Polish and Spanish**. English is the default, and you can switch the language with one click in `/setup`.
fields: 📜 Promo codes that work in the game

- A new code with a form in `/setup-roblox` → **📜 Promo codes** or the `/code-add` command: validity and rewards (currency, EXP, a permanent or timed item, e.g. VIP for 24 h).
- Codes reach the game **in a few seconds**, without publishing a game update (Roblox Open Cloud).
- `/code-remove` removes one code or several at once from a list. `/codes` shows players the active codes.
- A ready file for Roblox Studio with a code window, double-redeem protection and automatic rewards.
- **🕹️ Control panel** in your team's channel: administrators and the roles they choose run the game with buttons (`/setup-roblox` → 🕹️ Control panel).
🧪 Inside your game

- A ready **code window** with a **Codes** button (English, Polish and Spanish), plus a template if you want your own look.
- A **⚙️ Manager** panel that only the game's owner sees: active codes, events, eggs with their chances, waiting gifts, your player data, settings you can change live, test tools and the kit's messages. The owner also **creates codes, events, eggs, gifts, announcements and bans right there**, and the game does it by itself, even when the bot is off.
- The **game catalog** (`DiscordCatalog`): one list of your game's exact names, so the bot refuses typos before a code that can't work is created.
👥 For players on Discord

- `/codes` – the active codes to type in the game.
- `/eggs` – eggs with their pets and chances.
- `/events` – the events running now.
- `/leaderboard` – the game's top players.
⚙️ Setup without editing files

- `/tutorial`: a step-by-step tutorial inside the bot, with a live view of what already works (✅/⚠️) and buttons that open the right panels.
- `/setup`: Discord: language, the bug report channel and the log channel, diagnostics and the list of the bot's servers.
- `/setup-roblox`: your game: game link, API key, Studio file, names from the game (the game reports them itself), the game catalog, codes and a check of everything.
- `/setup-roblox` also has the panels for eggs, events, gifts, on-screen announcements, bans, the player card, the leaderboard and the control panel.
- `/setup-guide`: a step-by-step guide in three languages.
- `/help`: the list of commands.
🔄 Updates and error reports

- You download a new version from the #buyers channel on the CodeHatch HQ Discord server (you get the 💎 Buyer role when you buy): you copy the new files over the old ones and your settings and data stay (`CHANGELOG.md` lists what changed). The bot window and the bottom of `/help` show your version, e.g. `CodeHatch 1.0.0`.
- Automatic error reports on your own bug report channel (`/setup` → Channels). They never leave your server.
- The log channel (`/setup` → Channels) records every change in the game made from Discord or from the ⚙️ Manager, with who made it. Changes made in the game while the bot was off are written there when it starts again.
🎮 Your game controlled from Discord

- **Eggs:** `/egg-create` puts an egg on a stand in the game: price, pets with chances, color, limited time. `/egg-edit` and `/egg-remove` change it live. It shows the exact chances, also during a luck event, and won't sell an egg to a player Roblox doesn't allow paid random items.
- **Events:** `/event-start` turns on multipliers on every server, e.g. 2x Coins, 2x EXP or more luck for rare pets, with a timer on the players' screens.
- **Gifts:** `/give` sends currency, EXP or an item to one player (by username or Roblox ID), no code needed. The **Send a gift** button in `/setup-roblox` first shows a draft where you add EXP and the item's time; nothing reaches the game before ✅. Offline players get it when they join.
- **Announcements:** `/announce-game` shows a message on the screen of every player. Write without links: Roblox hides a whole text with a link (####).
- **Bans:** `/roblox-ban`, `/roblox-unban` and `/roblox-ban-check` work on every server through Roblox's official ban API.
- **Leaderboard:** `/leaderboard` shows the top players from the leaderboard your game already saves (an OrderedDataStore). The bot only reads it.
🔌 Your game works without the bot

Codes, eggs, events and gifts are saved in your game, so they keep working when the bot is off (your computer is asleep, the bot window is closed). The game's **⚙️ Manager** doesn't need the bot at all: in your game you create and remove codes, eggs, events, gifts, announcements and bans by yourself. The bot is needed only for Discord: the `/` commands, the panels and the log channel (the changes made in the game while it was off are written there when it starts). So you don't have to keep the bot online 24/7: it's a convenience.

sections.title: What you need and Python
sections.menu: Preparing your computer, once
sections.intro: You do this chapter once per computer. **You don't need to know how to code.** Do the steps in order and don't skip any.
fields: What you need

- a Windows computer (or Linux, or a bot hosting),
- a Discord account and your own Discord server where you are an administrator,
- a Roblox game you can edit in Roblox Studio,
- the bot's ZIP file (you get it in your Purchase ticket on the CodeHatch HQ Discord server).
Unzip the bot package

1. Right-click the ZIP file (`CodeHatch-1.0.0.zip`) → **Extract All…**.
2. Choose a folder that stays, e.g. `C:\Bots`, and click **Extract**.
3. Open the extracted folder, then the `CodeHatch-1.0.0` folder inside it: among others you'll see `start.bat`, `main.py` and `DOCS.html`. That's your bot folder.

Don't run anything straight from the ZIP preview: unzip it first. Don't put the bot folder in **OneDrive** or **Dropbox** (on many computers the Desktop and Documents are synced by OneDrive): they lock files while the bot uses them. `C:\Bots` is a safe place.
Install Python (once per computer)

The bot is tested on **Python 3.14**; 3.12 and 3.13 work too. Install it from **python.org**, not from the Microsoft Store.
1. Go to **python.org** → **Downloads** → **Windows**.
2. Under the newest Python 3.14 click **Windows installer (64-bit)** and run the downloaded file.
3. **On the first screen tick “Add python.exe to PATH” at the bottom**, then click **Install Now**. At the end you'll see *Setup was successful* → **Close**.
4. Done. You don't open anything in it: the bot starts it by itself.

Already have an older Python (3.10 or 3.11)? The bot starts with it too, but 3.12–3.14 is recommended. A Python newer than 3.14 hasn't been tested yet.

sections.title: The bot account on Discord
sections.menu: Application, intent and token
sections.intro: The bot needs its own Discord account. You create it once, on Discord's developer website. The program in the bot folder will “drive” that account.
fields: 1. New application

1. Go to **discord.com/developers/applications** and sign in.
2. **New Application** → type a name (e.g. your game's name) → tick the agreement → **Create**.

You'll see your new application's page. Already made one before? Open it from the list instead of creating another.
2. Intent and token

**Bot** tab:
- turn on **Server Members Intent** → **Save Changes** (the other two intents, Presence and Message Content, are not needed),
- click **Reset Token** → **Yes, do it!** → **Copy**. That's the bot token: you'll paste it into `.env` in a moment.
⚠️ The token is the bot's password
You put it only into the `.env` file. **Never send it to anyone**, not even someone who is helping you. If it leaks, click **Reset Token** again and paste the new one.
Private bot

**discord.com/developers/applications** → your app → first **Installation**: set **Install Link** to **None** and untick **User Install** → **Save Changes**; then **Bot** → turn **Public Bot** off → **Save Changes**. In this order: with an Install Link set, Discord refuses with “Private application cannot have a default authorization link”. You still invite the bot with the OAuth2 → URL Generator link. The bot works only on your servers anyway (it leaves strangers' servers by itself), but this way nobody can even try to add it. `/setup` → **🌐 Servers** shows the list: a server is added by itself when you (the account that created the bot) own it or have **Administrator** or **Manage Server** there.

**The bot's servers.** The bot's settings are shared by all its servers, so it works only on its owner's servers (the Discord account that created the bot in the Developer Portal); from any other server it leaves by itself. Only the bot's owner can change the list (`/setup` → **🌐 The bot's servers**):
- **Add a server ID** lets you add a server BEFORE you invite the bot there, e.g. a friend's server where you have no rights. A server ID has 17–20 digits. Get it: Discord → ⚙️ **User Settings** → **Advanced** → turn on **Developer Mode**, then right-click the server → **Copy Server ID**. You'll see ✅ *Server … was added*. Now invite the bot there: it stays.
- The **Remove a server (bot leaves)** list removes a server from the list and the bot leaves it.
- The window also warns you when **Public Bot** is on (follow the *Private bot* steps above).

sections.title: First start
sections.menu: start.bat and the .env file
sections.intro: Now you start the bot for the first time. Keep the token from the previous step at hand (if it's gone from the clipboard, click **Reset Token** again).
fields: 1. Run start.bat

1. Open the unzipped bot folder (the one with `start.bat`, `main.py` and `DOCS.html`).
2. Double-click **`start.bat`**. A black window opens: that's the bot's program (its messages are in English).
3. Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”? Click **More info** → **Run anyway**.

The first time, the bot prepares the Python environment and then opens Notepad with the `.env` file (it's made from `.env.example`, the template in the zip).
2. Paste the token into .env

In Notepad you'll see the line `DISCORD_TOKEN=your_bot_token_here`. Select and delete `your_bot_token_here` and paste the token in its place (**Ctrl+V**). Keep `DISCORD_TOKEN=` as it is, with no spaces or quotes, e.g. `DISCORD_TOKEN=MTI3NDk…`.
3. Save and wait

Save the file (**Ctrl+S**) and close Notepad. The bot now installs its libraries: for a few minutes the window may look frozen, that's normal. When `✅ Synced … commands` shows up, the bot works. The window also shows a block with `📦 CodeHatch 1.0.0` (your version) and `🎮 The bot is ONLINE!`. **Don't close this window**: closing it turns the bot off.

Normal at the first start:
- `⚠️ "Public Bot" is ON in the Discord Developer Portal…`: just a reminder. The bot works; make it private later (chapter *The bot account on Discord* → *Private bot*).
- Clicking into the window doesn't pause the bot (it turns Windows' select mode off). If the window title still starts with *Select*, press **Esc**.
Getting back to .env and restarting the bot

- **Open `.env` again:** in the bot folder right-click `.env` → **Open with** → **Notepad**.
- **Restart the bot:** close the black window and double-click `start.bat`.

Restart the bot after every change in `.env`.
Linux or a server

- **Linux / macOS / server:** `bash start.sh` (the same, but without Notepad; fill in `.env` with `nano .env`).
- Manually: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then `python main.py` (after every update run `pip install -r requirements.txt` again).
💡 Your own files

Three things in the bot folder are yours: `.env` (token and keys), `config.json` (settings) and the `data` folder (database: codes, eggs, events, gifts). Copy them somewhere safe from time to time and **never overwrite them** when you update the bot. Moving to another computer or host is fine: copy the whole folder.

sections.title: Invite the bot to your server
sections.menu: A link with permissions and the bot's role
sections.intro: The bot runs, now it has to join your Discord server.
fields: The invite link

1. Developer Portal → your application → **OAuth2** → **URL Generator**.
2. Under *Scopes* tick **bot** and **applications.commands**.
3. Below, under *Bot Permissions*, tick **View Channels**, **Send Messages**, **Embed Links** and **Read Message History** (the card *Which permissions the bot needs* explains why). Don't tick **Administrator**: the bot doesn't need it.
4. Copy the link at the bottom, open it in your browser, pick your server → **Authorize**.

The bot appears in your server's member list.
Which permissions the bot needs

Only four: **View Channels**, **Send Messages**, **Embed Links** and **Read Message History**. That's all the bot needs: it doesn't give roles and doesn't moderate members, so it never needs **Administrator**. Without these four it can't post its panels and error reports. Invited it with Administrator earlier? It works, but you can take it away: Server Settings → **Roles** → the bot's role → **Permissions** → turn on the four above, turn off **Administrator** → **Save Changes**.
First command: /tutorial

On your server type **`/tutorial`**. The bot walks you through everything else, chapter by chapter: it shows what already works (✅) and what is missing (⚠️), and the green buttons open exactly the place being explained.

`/` commands can take a few minutes to show up. If you don't see them, press **Ctrl+R** in Discord.
The bot starts in English

At first the bot speaks English: the welcome “👋 Thanks for adding me!” it posts on the server and `/tutorial` too. To change it: `/setup` → the **🌐 Language / Język / Idioma** list at the very bottom. It works right away.
✅ How to check it worked
The bot shows as online in the server's member list, and `/tutorial` → chapter 2 (*The bot on your server: permissions*) shows ✅ for the permissions.

sections.title: Problems at the start
sections.menu: Black window, token, commands
sections.intro: The most common troubles on the first start and how to fix them. The messages below are written exactly as the black window shows them: `start.bat` always speaks English, the bot itself speaks the bot's language (English at first).
fields: `ERROR: Python was not found.`
Python isn't installed, or “Add python.exe to PATH” wasn't ticked. Install it again from python.org with that option ticked (chapter *What you need and Python*) and double-click `start.bat` again.
`ERROR: The bot needs Python 3.10 or newer, but an older Python was found`

Windows found an old Python, or only the Microsoft Store shortcut. Install Python 3.14 from **python.org** (chapter *What you need and Python*), with “Add python.exe to PATH” ticked, and run `start.bat` again.
`ERROR: Could not create the Python environment.` or `ERROR: Could not install the libraries. Check your internet connection.`

Check your internet connection and double-click `start.bat` again. Still failing? Install Python 3.13 or 3.14 from **python.org** (not from the Microsoft Store), delete the `.venv` folder in the bot folder and run `start.bat` again. Also make sure the bot folder isn't in OneDrive or Dropbox.
`The Python environment in the .venv folder is incomplete: creating it again...`

That's fine: an earlier start broke off, and `start.bat` repairs the `.venv` folder by itself. Wait. Only if it then says `ERROR: The Python environment can't be created with pip.`, install Python again from python.org, delete the `.venv` folder and run `start.bat` again.
`ERROR: The .env file has no bot token yet (DISCORD_TOKEN).` or `❌ ERROR: No valid DISCORD_TOKEN in the .env file!`

There's no token in `.env`: the text `your_bot_token_here` is still there, or the file wasn't saved. Open `.env` (chapter *First start*, “Getting back to .env”), paste the token in place of that text, save and run `start.bat` again.
`❌ Discord didn't accept the bot token (DISCORD_TOKEN in .env).`

The token in `.env` is wrong or out of date: Developer Portal → your app → **Bot** → **Reset Token** → **Copy**, paste the new one into `.env` after `DISCORD_TOKEN=` (no spaces or quotes), save and start the bot again.
`❌ Discord refused the connection: the bot needs one intent.`
The intent isn't on: Developer Portal → your application → **Bot** tab → turn on **Server Members Intent** → **Save Changes**, then start the bot again.
`⚠️ "Public Bot" is ON in the Discord Developer Portal…`
Normal on the first start, not an error: the bot works. It's a reminder to make the bot private when you have a moment (chapter *The bot account on Discord* → *Private bot*).
`⚠️ No connection to Discord (…). Trying again in … s...`
No internet, or Discord has a short outage. Nothing to do: the bot waits and tries again by itself.
The black window stopped moving

The bot turns off the window's select mode, so a click into it doesn't pause the bot. If the window title still starts with *Select*, press **Esc**. A bot folder in OneDrive or Dropbox can also make it hang: move the folder to e.g. `C:\Bots`.
I don't see the `/` commands
Wait a few minutes and press **Ctrl+R** in Discord. Check that the bot is on the server (invited with the **applications.commands** scope) and that the black window is open.
A moderator gets “You don't have permission”

Panels (`/setup`, `/setup-roblox`) and admin commands work only for people with **Administrator** (or the server owner). Allowing the command for another role in **Server Settings → Integrations** only shows it on the list: the bot still checks the permissions itself, so nobody gets past them. Give the person a role with *Administrator* or do the change yourself.
“The application did not respond”

The bot isn't running: the black window is closed, the computer is asleep, or the bot stopped with an error (see what the black window says). Run `start.bat` again. To keep it running all the time: the quest *Bot 24/7*.
The bot can't post in a channel

The channel hides itself from the bot. Channel → ⚙️ **Edit Channel** → **Permissions** → add the bot's role and allow **View Channel**, **Send Messages** and **Embed Links**. `/setup` → **🩺 Diagnostics** shows what is missing.
Something doesn't work in the game (e.g. codes)
`/setup-roblox` → **🧪 Check everything** tells you what is missing. More: *Codes in game: problems*.
`❌ This bot is already running` or `This bot is already running in another window.`
Another copy of the bot is running (another `start.bat` window, or a hosting panel). Two copies would answer everything twice, so the second one stops. Close the other window.
`❌ config.json can't be read`

The file was edited by hand and has a mistake (usually a missing comma or quote). The message says the line. Fix it in Notepad, or put back your copy, and start the bot again. Nothing was changed by the bot.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.menu: Tricky words explained once
sections.intro: Words that show up in the instructions. Read them once and the rest gets easier.
fields: Discord application / bot
The bot account you create on Discord's website. The program in this folder “drives” that account.
Bot token
The bot's password. You put it only into the `.env` file. **Never send it to anyone** (not even someone who is helping you).
Application ID
Your bot's number (Developer Portal → your app → **General Information**). It isn't secret, and the invite link from **OAuth2 → URL Generator** already contains it.
Intent
A switch on Discord's developer website (your app → **Bot** tab) that lets the bot see certain information. This bot needs only one: **Server Members Intent**.
Bug report channel
A private channel on your server where the bot posts reports about its own errors. You pick it in `/setup` → **📡 Channels**.
`.env`
The file with secret keys in the bot folder. You open it with Notepad.
`/` command
On Discord type a slash `/` and the name, e.g. `/tutorial`, then Enter.
Game link
Your game's address from the browser, e.g. `https://www.roblox.com/games/123456789/Name`. The bot reads the Place ID and Universe ID from it.
API key (Open Cloud)
A key from Roblox Creator Hub that lets the bot change your game's data (e.g. promo codes).
Roblox Studio
The program where you edit your game.
Explorer

The Studio window that lists everything in the game (Workspace, Players, ServerScriptService…). It's usually on the right. Don't see it? **Window** menu → **Explorer** (or the **Explorer** button on the **Home** tab).
Properties
The Studio window with the settings of the selected thing (color, text, size…). Open it the same way: **Window** menu → **Properties** (or the button on the **Home** tab).
Output
The Studio window where the game writes messages, including the bot's (`[DiscordCodes] …`). Don't see it? **Window** menu → **Output**.
Play and Publish
**Play** runs the game as a test in Studio, only for you. **Publish** (**File → Publish to Roblox**, Alt+P) sends players the whole game open in Studio.
Experience Settings

The game's settings in Studio: **File** menu → **Experience Settings** (older Studio: **Home** → **Game Settings**). This is where you turn on **Security** → **Enable Studio Access to API Services**, among others.
ServerStorage and StarterGui
More folders in the **Explorer** window. Scripts in **ServerStorage** don't run, so it's where you keep a backup. **StarterGui** holds the windows and buttons a player sees.
Place
One place (map) of your game. Most games have one; a game with several places needs the bot's file in every place where players type codes.
leaderstats

A folder in player data where many games keep the currency and points shown in the player list. That's where the bot gives rewards. In games with their own save system (e.g. ProfileStore) it's only a copy: see *Rewards: for the game's developer*.
Black window
The command window that `start.bat` opens. It's the running bot: `start.bat` writes in English, the bot in its own language, and closing the window turns the bot off.
ServerScriptService
A folder in Studio (in the **Explorer** window) for scripts that run on the game server.
`DiscordCodes.rbxmx`
One file from the bot's `scripts` folder that you insert into your game. It lets the game understand commands from Discord.
`DiscordSettings.rbxmx`

An optional file from the same `scripts` folder with your settings: the **Codes** button, the language, a currency limit per code, the ⚙️ Manager panel. You insert it once next to DiscordCodes, and updates never change it.

sections.title: Bot updates
sections.menu: Your version, the new zip, what to keep, CHANGELOG
sections.intro: You copy the new files over the old ones, and your token, settings and database stay as they are. It takes a few minutes.
fields: 0. Which version do I have?
When the bot starts, its window shows `📦 CodeHatch 1.0.0`; the bottom of `/help` on Discord shows it too. After an update the bot writes *🔄 The bot was updated from version … to …*.
Where do I get a new version?
On the CodeHatch HQ Discord server, in the #buyers channel (you see it with the 💎 Buyer role you got when you bought the bot): download the newest zip (e.g. `CodeHatch-1.0.1.zip`).
1. See what changed

Unzip the new version (right-click → **Extract All…**) to a new folder, e.g. `C:\Bots-new`, and open the file **`CHANGELOG.md`** in it with Notepad. Read **every entry between your version and the new one**, not only the top one: if you skipped a version, its steps (e.g. replacing the Studio file) still apply. It lists what is new and whether the Roblox Studio file `DiscordCodes.rbxmx` changed.
2. Make a backup (just in case)

Copy your whole bot folder somewhere else, e.g. as `C:\Bots-backup`. If you're short on space, copy at least `.env`, `config.json` and the `data` folder: that is all your data (token and keys, settings, the database with codes, eggs, events and gifts).
3. Close the bot
Close the black window (on a hosting: stop the bot in the panel). Don't copy files while the bot is running.
4. Copy the new files

1. Open the unzipped new version, select everything inside (**Ctrl+A**) and copy it (**Ctrl+C**). You'll see one folder there (e.g. `CodeHatch-1.0.1`): open it first.
2. Open your bot folder (the one with `start.bat`) and paste (**Ctrl+V**).
3. Windows asks about files with the same names: choose **Replace the files in the destination**.

**Never overwrite** `.env`, `config.json` or the `data` folder. If the new version has a file or folder with one of these names, don't copy it.
5. Start the bot again

Double-click **`start.bat`** (Linux: `bash start.sh`). It installs new libraries by itself, so the first start can take a minute or two. When a line with ✅ shows up (`Synced … commands` or `Slash commands are up to date`), the new version works. The bot also writes *🔄 The bot was updated from version … to …* in the window and on your log channel. New settings are added to `config.json` by themselves, and when the database needs changes, the bot first saves a copy in `data/backups`.
📥 The Roblox Studio file

**The file `scripts/DiscordCodes.rbxmx` is not replaced inside your game automatically.** When an update changes it, `CHANGELOG.md` says so and `/setup-roblox` shows ⚠️ next to the DiscordCodes file. Only then do the next checkpoint (*Updating the Studio file*). If neither says anything about it, you can skip that step.
Files you changed by hand

The new version replaces the files in `locales/` (texts) and `scripts/`. If you changed something there yourself, make the same change again after the update. Your own scripts inside your Roblox game are not affected.
Something went wrong?

1. Read what the black window says and look for it in *Problems at the start*.
2. To go back to the old version: close the bot, rename the bot folder (e.g. to `Bot-new`), give your backup copy the old folder's name and start `start.bat` in it.
3. Questions: the project's GitHub Issues page. Attach the file `data/logs/bot.log` (tokens and keys are hidden in it).
